source.title: Low-Dimensional and Transversely Curved Optimization Dynamics in Grokking

record.tranche_reason: The study trains small transformers on modular-arithmetic tasks and measures test-accuracy transitions, but investigates them with geometric diagnostics and a different experimental setup rather than reproducing the original method in full.
record.gate_note: The study reports grokking outcomes on modular arithmetic and measures geometric signals around the transition. It does not report a training-set-size sweep. Its commutator and spectral measurements are not direct measurements of Fourier-circuit formation or removal of memorizing components. Some figures are described in text, but their precise plotted values are not stated.
record.test_reason: The study reruns the canonical Power et al. setup: a small transformer on modular arithmetic mod 97, reading test accuracy over steps. Its grok-step results across operations, learning rates and a slow regime bear directly on V1, at a single 50/50 split. Its geometric diagnostics (commutator defect, PCA, weight SVD) measure other constructs and do not test V2–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right but incomplete. The authors' central thesis is that grokking is prolonged confinement to a rank-1, empirically invariant weight subspace (PC1 68–83%), while curvature accumulates orthogonally, until escape. Defect onset precedes generalization but is necessary, not sufficient. Suppressing orthogonal gradient flow prevents grokking, and boosting defect does nothing. A σ1≈σ2 near-degeneracy and its breaking in attention matrices is the proposed mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a canonical small-transformer modular-arithmetic setup with a 50/50 split, but uses its stated architecture, AdamW settings, weight decay, and geometric measurements rather than reproducing the original study's full method. No training-set-size sweep is reported.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports changes across task, learning rate, weight decay, model depth and Adam β2 regime, seed, and intervention strength. It says alignment dynamics differ quantitatively between fast and slow regimes and vary with learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Commutator-defect onset precedes 90% test accuracy by 600–1600 steps (sign test p≈2.4×10−4). Lead time scales as t_grok^1.27 across learning rates. Non-grokking operations also show 30–50x defect growth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A loss-curvature (gradient non-commutativity) signal rises before grokking but does not discriminate which runs will generalize.

fits_no_version.finding: The weight-matrix spectral gap g23 declines before grokking in 12/12 weight-decay runs versus 1/12 no-wd controls, followed by σ1≈σ2 degeneracy and then symmetry breaking at generalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking is preceded by a spectral near-degeneracy and symmetry breaking in the attention weight matrices.

fits_no_version.finding: Restricting gradients to the learned PCA subspace delays or prevents grokking, but random projections also prevent it at full strength. Commutator-aligned kicks do not accelerate grokking (27/27 runs).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Motion along learned low-dimensional directions is associated with grokking, and inducing curvature alone does not trigger it.

record.problems: The experiments are limited to small transformers and synthetic modular arithmetic. Training accuracy is not reported numerically in the presented results, and training-set size is not varied. Several plotted measurements are described qualitatively rather than supplied as exact values. The authors also state that the geometric diagnostics do not prospectively distinguish grokking from non-grokking operations.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately stated numerical or explicit behavioral outcomes bearing on the tested version were omitted. Geometric measurements and intervention results are included as findings outside the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size: only a 50/50 split is used. Training-accuracy saturation is asserted but not reported numerically.

All parts: no Fourier or other circuit is identified, no circuit progress measure is taken, and no removal of memorizing components is measured. The commutator and spectral signals are other constructs.
All parts: only modular arithmetic is tested (Dyck and SCAN are mentioned as preliminary, no results), and initialization scale and lazy-to-rich transitions are not manipulated.
All parts: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Efficiency comparison of circuits, critical dataset size, and ungrokking are untested. Only the dependence of grokking on weight decay is shown.
All parts: learned algorithms are not compared across runs.
All parts: AdamW is used throughout, with no optimizer or floating-point controls.

missing.what: No-weight-decay (λ=0) controls on the four grokking operations: the runs memorize but do not grok (1/12 late exception at step 41,700).
missing.versions: V1 (scope condition); V5 (weight-decay dependence only, not the efficiency account)

missing.what: At η ≥ 3×10−3, grokking takes under 1k steps and memorization and generalization overlap, so there is no delayed generalization.
Per-learning-rate mean grok steps (e.g. ~30k at η=10−4) and grok fractions from the 108-run sweep.

record.verdict_notes: Single-author preprint building on the author's own prior work. V1 support comes from a single 50% split with modest delays (~6x memorization time), far smaller than in the original data-fraction sweeps. The 'necessity' causal claim is weakened because random 16-dimensional projections also block grokking at s=1.0. The record's reader labelled r11 and r13 with states describing V1-like outcomes, though they are unlinked geometric or intervention results; this has been corrected above.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not vary training-set size, so it does not test whether smaller training sets require more optimization. It describes memorization before generalization but does not report training-accuracy values demonstrating perfect training accuracy.
The study does not measure formation of a Fourier or other generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or a progress measure of that circuit.
Only synthetic modular-arithmetic tasks are studied; no non-algorithmic datasets or lazy-to-rich initialization or weight-norm transition is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
Although weight-decay settings are compared, the study does not test whether low norm selects a more efficient circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
The study does not identify and compare the algorithms learned across runs.
The study does not test whether grokking is an optimizer or numerical artifact, or whether controlling such effects removes it.

rows.measure: Step at which test accuracy reaches 90% (grok step)
rows.note: The table reports a mean over 3 seeds. The study defines grokking as test accuracy reaching 98% for 3 consecutive evaluations; it uses 90% for the reported grok step.
rows.check: Grok step uses a 90% test-accuracy threshold. Memorization (~step 500, Section 4.7.1) is implied, but training accuracy is not reported numerically. The delay here is modest (~6x), at a single 50% split.

rows.subject: 2-layer Transformer encoder, approximately 290k parameters
rows.operation_detail: Sweep learning rate and report the range of mean grok steps.
rows.note: The study states that the same four operations grok at all six tested rates and the two complex operations never grok.
rows.check: Grokking occurs at all six learning rates. However, at η ≥ 3×10−3 the text says grokking takes under 1k steps and memorization and generalization overlap, so the delayed-generalization part of V1 is absent there. The row records only the grok-step range.

rows.subject: Transformer encoder, modular addition, seed 42
rows.operation_detail: Track test accuracy during training in the representative spectral-timeline run.
rows.value: Test accuracy remains at chance through the competition and instability phases and rises as the trajectory enters the alignment region; grok step 3100.
rows.note: The text gives the ordered spectral events at steps 1400, 1700, 2000, 2700, 2800, and grok at 3100.
rows.check: Single-seed illustration (seed 42, layer 0). Chance-level test accuracy is described from the figure, not given as a number.

rows.subject: 2-layer Transformer encoder, approximately 290k parameters
rows.operation_detail: Measure commutator-defect onset relative to the test-accuracy transition.
rows.measure: Lead time from defect onset to test accuracy reaching 90%
rows.note: Defect onset is defined using a 10× early-training baseline and an absolute threshold of 20.
rows.check: Commutator-defect lead time is a geometric curvature proxy, not a progress measure of a generalizing circuit. Correctly unlinked from V2.

rows.subject: 2-layer Transformer encoder, approximately 290k parameters
rows.operation_detail: Measure commutator-defect growth on operations that do not generalize.

conditions.value: (a2 + ab + b2) mod 97 and (a3 + ab) mod 97

rows.measure: Defect growth relative to early-training baseline and test accuracy
rows.value: Defect reaches 30–50× baseline, but the operations never generalize; maximum test accuracy is below 78%.
rows.note: The study says early defect trajectories overlap between grokking and non-grokking operations.
rows.check: State should describe the defect result itself: defect growth of 30–50x occurs without generalization. It is not 'absent' on any version. Correctly unlinked.

rows.subject: 2-layer Transformer encoder, approximately 290k parameters
rows.operation_detail: Suppress gradients orthogonal to the PCA subspace after step 500.
rows.note: This is an induced gradient constraint, rather than unmodified training.
rows.check: Training intervention designed by the study. At s=1.0, random projections also prevent grokking, so this result is not specific to the PCA directions.

rows.subject: 2-layer Transformer encoder, approximately 290k parameters
rows.operation_detail: Apply partial gradient suppression along the PCA subspace.
rows.measure: Delay in grok step relative to baseline
rows.note: The study reports this delay across all four operations.
rows.check: Study's own intervention. The delay of 600–800 steps is the measured effect, so 'partial' mislabels it.

rows.subject: 2-layer Transformer encoder, approximately 290k parameters
rows.operation_detail: Apply random low-dimensional gradient projections as a control.
rows.note: At s = 1.0, the study says both PCA and random projections prevent grokking.

rows.subject: 2-layer Transformer encoder, approximately 290k parameters
rows.operation_detail: Inject periodic weight updates along the commutator direction or random orthogonal directions.
rows.value: Neither kick type accelerates grokking; all 27/27 runs generalize at statistically indistinguishable times (∼3200 steps, within seed-to-seed variability).
rows.note: The study interprets this as evidence that increasing defect alone is insufficient.
rows.check: Study's own intervention; fine as unlinked.

relationships.condition: Four operations (add, sub, mul, a²+b²) mod 97 at 50/50 split, wd=1.0, η=10−3 to 10−4 range, and slow regime (3 layers, wd=0.1)
relationships.reason: Test accuracy stays at chance after memorization, then rises to ≥98% at grok steps ~1900–3400 (fast) or ~570k (slow), in 12/12 and 2/2 runs (r1–r4, r7, r9, r8 at low η).
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy rose from chance after memorization to at least 98% around steps 1,900–3,400 in all 12 fast runs and around 570,000 in both slow runs.

tranche.reason: The study reruns the canonical small-transformer modular-arithmetic training method and measures held-out accuracy over training. Its additional geometric diagnostics do not change the method and measure underlying the V1 results.
